findings.reason: the plan must name the unit-conversion owner (extend the engine to compile the unit factor, or a shared unit module) and stop asserting a factor the engine does not compile.
findings.text: `_unit_factor` and its `_UNIT_CONVERSIONS` table (imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py:101) are the only unit-conversion implementation in ambix, while the transform engine applies no unit factor at all (imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:78-89 `EmittedArray` carries `source_unit`/`target_unit` as metadata and the transform applies only `cocos_factor`, lines 447-477); so §2's stated mechanism for `jtmm-tokamap-jt60sa` — take "each binding's factor from the engine's own resolution" and assert the exported `scale` against "the engine's compiled factor" — would silently drop the unit half of the collapsed scale, and §6's unit-audit done-when ("every binding's source and target units resolve through the DD unit vocabulary with the derived factor asserted") has no resolver to resolve against.

findings.reason: the author should extend the owner (transform_engine) with a named public per-binding resolution the exporter consumes, closing the duplicate and the private-symbol dependency in one change.
findings.text: the DD-path COCOS-label lookup exists twice with byte-identical logic over `cocos_label_transformation`: `_target_cocos_transformation` at imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:411 and `_cocos_transformation` at imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py:147; the plan names retiring the exporter copy, but the owner (transform_engine) exposes no public resolution for a binding's compiled factor — both resolvers are private and the factor path (`_apply_cocos_convention` line 447, `_apply_sign_convention` line 396, `_poloidal_angle_sense_factor` line 425) is private too, so the retirement will either import a private symbol or re-fork the lookup, and §2's interface account does not name the public entry point.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new public entry hides substantial behaviour behind it (imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py export_tokamap_directory collapses unit·sign·COCOS into one scale; imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py read_signal_map_observation hides rule resolution and interpolation behind one call), and the EQDB work extends the existing transport's dispatch rather than widening its channel types.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan assumes an engine-side factor resolution the engine does not perform for units, and does not name the owner for the unit-conversion mechanism §6's unit audit needs.
rubric_items.interface_budget: public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 — pass; each section that adds a public name states what it retires or why nothing can be (the §2 seven exporter names, the §6 three EQDB types and measure_convention, the §7 pin table and the JT-60SA shot-set identity all carry that account).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and cites the mechanism it extends at each proposal (imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py score_convention, imas_ambix/challenge/convention.py _integrated_current, imas_ambix/gs/operator.py assemble_pf_currents, imas_ambix/gs/machine_identity.py default_registry, imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py pins, imas_ambix/data/eddb.py store, imas_ambix/data/paths.py JT60SA_ROOT), so it does not rebuild a subsystem it did not search for.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two adapters the plan adds route through existing seams and say so: the SELENE reference reduction goes through imas_ambix/worldmodel/equilibrium_labels.py build_geometry_from_arrays behind eval/efit_referee.py read_efit_geometry(loader=...), and the machine pin read goes through the selector, rather than wrapping a second read path.
